title: In a Cohen-Macaulay local ring, elements cutting the dimension by their number form a regular sequence
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) whose Krull dimension $d=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is finite, and assume that $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak m$ contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $d$. Let $c\ge0$ be an integer and $g_1,\dots,g_c\in\mathfrak m$ elements such that the ring $R/(g_1,\dots,g_c)$ has Krull dimension $\dim R/(g_1,\dots,g_c)=d-c$. Then $g_1,\dots,g_c$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), first assertion, for the module M = R (the support of R/(g_1,...,g_c) is V(g_1,...,g_c), of dimension dim R/(g_1,...,g_c)); Cohen-Macaulay as in Definition Tag 00N3 (definition-CM, line 24960: dim Supp(M) = depth(M)), here depth(R) >= dim R, equivalent since the depth never exceeds the dimension

proof.text: Work with finite modules over R and their quotients. Mathlib Submodule.quotOfListConsSMulTopEquivQuotSMulTopInner identifies M/(g::gs)M with (M/gM)/(gs)(M/gM); Module.supportDim_eq_of_equiv transports support dimension. The empty-list quotient is M via Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot. Supports use the module-localization convention. For M = R, Module.supportDim_self_eq_ringKrullDim and Module.supportDim_quotient_eq_ringKrullDim identify support dimensions with ring dimensions, using the finite-module support-annihilator correspondence.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6, first paragraph of proof; induction on the list with the quotient identifications supplied by Mathlib

proof.text: The private proved helper supportDim_le_quotient_add_length inducts on gs, generalizing the finite module M. Its empty case is the quotient equivalence from step 1. In the cons case, 0B52 gives dim Supp M <= dim Supp(M/gM)+1; the induction hypothesis gives dim Supp(M/gM) <= dim Supp(M/(g::gs)M)+length gs. Add the inequalities to obtain dim Supp M <= dim Supp(M/(gs)M)+length gs. No nonzero assumption is needed in this helper.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6, first paragraph of proof; induction on the list with the quotient identifications supplied by Mathlib

proof.text: Use depth_le_supportDim on the nonzero finite module R. Since supportDim R R = dim R = d and d <= depth R, antisymmetry gives depth R = supportDim R R. This is Cohen-Macaulayness. The given ring dimension equality becomes supportDim R (R/(gs)R)+length gs = supportDim R R.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6, first paragraph of proof; induction on the list with the quotient identifications supplied by Mathlib

proof.text: The private proved helper isRegular_of_cm_dimension_drop inducts on gs, generalizing the nonzero finite Cohen-Macaulay module M. The empty case is IsRegular.nil. For g::gs put Q=M/gM. Step 2 for Q and gs, together with the final dimension equality, implies dim Supp Q+1 <= dim Supp M. The one-element 0B52 inequality gives the reverse inequality, hence dim Supp Q+1 = dim Supp M. Module.support_quotSMulTop rewrites Supp Q as Supp M intersect V(g), so the existing one-element Cohen-Macaulay theorem applies. It gives g regular on M and Q Cohen-Macaulay.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6, first paragraph of proof; induction on the list with the quotient identifications supplied by Mathlib

proof.text: Q is nonzero by Nakayama: maximalIdeal R is contained in the Jacobson radical of the annihilator of M, so Submodule.top_ne_pointwise_smul_of_mem_jacobson_annihilator shows gM is not M. Cancel addition of 1 in WithBot ENat (ENat.WithBot.add_one_cancel) between the final dimension equality and dim Supp Q+1 = dim Supp M. This gives the final dimension equality for gs on Q. Apply the induction hypothesis to get IsRegular Q gs and combine it with g regular on M using isRegular_cons_iff. Finally specialize this helper to M=R using step 3.

lean.statement: theorem isRegular_of_dimension_drop {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim R = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hdepth : (d : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := R) R) (gs : List R) (hmem : ∀ g ∈ gs, g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hdrop : ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList gs) + (gs.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) : IsRegular R gs

reviewed_lean.note: Noetherian local R; d:ℕ with ringKrullDim R = d (finite dim); CM inline as d ≤ IsLocalRing.depth R (as H1 e10ccd492); gs : List R, c = length; all g ∈ maximalIdeal; dim R⧸Ideal.ofList gs (reducible = Ideal.span {r | r ∈ gs}) + c = d in WithBot ℕ∞ (= integer d-c, quotient nonzero so no ⊥/⊤ case); conclusion Mathlib RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R gs (weakly regular + final quotient nonzero); #check clean
